text:
Diego Santos: Dropping ADR draft for Private backup format + encryption. Need eyes from Security/Reliability/Compliance before we mark it accepted. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/ARCH/ADR-0137-private-backup-format-and-encryption (draft)

Diego Santos: TL;DR proposal:
- Backup artifact = chunked `tar` stream compressed w/ `zstd` (fixed chunk size), plus `manifest.json`.
- Encryption = envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM per chunk). Data key generated per-backup, wrapped by customer KMS/HSM where available.
- If object storage supports SSE-KMS we can use that too, but ADR assumes we can’t rely on it (NFS/minio/airgap).
- Integrity = SHA-256 per chunk in manifest + overall manifest hash.

Marcus Lin: Reading now. First reaction: we should be super explicit on key ownership + threat model.
1) Redwood should never require plaintext KEK/CMK material (only calls to KMS). Put that in “non-goals/constraints”.
2) Define where DEK exists in memory (job pod only) + log redaction requirements.
3) Call out: for air-gapped, “KMS” could be HSM or offline key ceremony — we need to say what we support vs what’s customer-run.

Miles Thornton: +1. Also can we define what “backup complete” means? If chunk upload partially fails, we need an atomic marker. Manifest should be last write and include total chunk count.

Ethan Park: On artifact schema: please add a section for control plane ordering / restore dependency.
- `control-plane-db` (postgres) dump/WAL
- `config-policy` (benji’s service)
- `secrets-certs` (only encrypted form)
- `object-store` pointers (model artifacts/logs)
Right now the schema reads like “one blob” which is fine, but restore sequencing depends on knowing which components are present.

Hanae Suzuki: Security nit: “secrets/certs” backup content needs precise language.
We can back up encrypted Kubernetes Secrets *if* we’re using customer-managed encryption-at-rest (KMS provider) OR we do explicit client-side encryption. But we should NOT imply we can export plaintext secrets.
Also: for TLS private keys, many customers keep them external (e.g., cert-manager + Vault). ADR should call out “external secret sources are out of scope” and we only back up references/metadata.

Olga Petrov: From compliance/evidence side: please add:
- What audit logs exist for backup create/verify/restore (at least “who initiated” + “backup id” + “target location”).
- Retention + immutability recommendations (WORM / object lock) as an appendix.
- Key rotation expectations (what happens to existing backups when CMK rotates).

Allison Grant: Observability: can we add to ADR that every backup has a stable `backup_id` used across:
- metrics labels
- manifest
- logs
This will help dashboards and the incident-bot shortcuts. Also: manifest should include start/end timestamps and tool version.

Diego Santos: Great feedback. Quick questions:
- Marcus: do we want AES-GCM per chunk w/ random nonce, store nonce in manifest, or derive nonce from chunk index?
- Miles: for atomic marker, we were thinking `manifest.json` last + `COMPLETED` sentinel object/file written last.

Marcus Lin: For nonce: do NOT derive from chunk index unless we can guarantee never reuse (same key + same nonce is catastrophic). Safer:
- random 96-bit nonce per chunk, stored alongside chunk metadata in manifest.
Also: please specify we generate a unique DEK per backup (not per cluster, not per day).

Miles Thornton: Sentinel file is fine if storage is POSIX-ish. For object storage, “manifest last” is usually enough *if* we require restore to only consider backups with valid manifest + all chunks present.
Add an explicit “incomplete backups are ignored” rule. That will save operators.

Connor O'Brien: +1 on ignoring incomplete. Also from release eng: ADR should specify forward compatibility:
- manifest includes `schema_version`
- tool writes both `schema_version` and `tool_version`
- restore refuses unknown major versions unless `--force`

Ethan Park: Another restore detail: include a “quiesce point” in manifest for DB backups.
If we’re doing PITR/WAL, we should record the LSN / end-of-backup marker in manifest so restore can validate.

Hanae Suzuki: Please add a line that backup job should run with minimal RBAC and never list/read Secrets unless explicitly configured. We’ve had customers ask “does your backup job scrape everything in the cluster?”

Diego Santos: Ok.
Proposed ADR edits:
- Add “Key ownership boundary” section: customer CMK/KEK only; Redwood uses KMS API; no plaintext keys in logs.
- Add “Nonce strategy” section: random nonce per chunk stored in manifest.
- Add “Artifact completeness + atomicity” section: manifest last; optional COMPLETED marker; restore ignores incomplete.
- Expand manifest schema: schema_version, tool_version, backup_id, start/end ts, chunk list {name,size,sha256,nonce}, components present, DB LSN.
- Add appendix for evidence/audit logs + retention/object-lock guidance.

Allison Grant: For metrics labeling: please keep `backup_id` high-cardinality out of Prometheus labels for steady-state metrics. We can log it + use it in events, but for metrics we likely want `cluster_id`, `namespace`, `backup_type` (scheduled/manual), and a gauge like “last_successful_backup_timestamp”.
Maybe ADR can say “backup_id present in events/logs, not required as metric label”.

Diego Santos: Good call. I’ll tweak that wording.

Marcus Lin: Another thing: encryption mode per storage backend.
We should state:
- For S3/GCS/Azure: client-side encryption always available; optionally enable SSE-KMS as defense-in-depth.
- For NFS/local bundle: client-side required.
- For minio: treat like S3 but don’t assume SSE-KMS exists.
And say “never depend solely on transport security” (TLS) for confidentiality.

Olga Petrov: Also add “verification” expectation: `backup verify` must validate:
- manifest signature/hash
- all chunks present
- sha256 match
- decrypt test (at least first chunk) without writing plaintext to disk
This is important for auditors: proof the backup is actually usable.

Ethan Park: +1 on decrypt test. For DB piece, verify should also check pg_dump file is non-empty and WAL archive has expected segment count (or at least presence).

Diego Santos: Ok updating ADR now. Will post when revised.

Diego Santos: Updated draft is up (same link). Changes:
- Added “Threat model + non-goals” section (no plaintext CMK/KEK, no exporting external vault secrets).
- Added “Format v1” section w/ explicit manifest schema + component inventory.
- Added “Encryption” section w/ envelope encryption flow + random nonce per chunk + DEK lifecycle.
- Added “Completeness + restore selection rules” (manifest last, ignore incomplete).
- Added “Verification requirements” and “Audit/evidence appendix”.
Please re-review 🙏

Marcus Lin: Read the diff. This is much better. One last request: explicitly say the encrypted DEK is stored in manifest as `wrapped_dek` and includes `kms_key_id`/`key_uri` but does NOT include any credentials. And say we support multiple wrap providers (aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure-kv, pkcs11).

Hanae Suzuki: Reviewed. The clarifications on secrets/certs are good. Please keep the language “we back up *Redwood-managed* secrets only” and “external secret sources are operator responsibility”.

Olga Petrov: Reviewed. Evidence appendix is solid. Can we add a sentence that game day artifacts should include the `backup verify` output + restore smoke test output? (helps standardize.)

Miles Thornton: Looks good now. Restore selection rules are exactly what we needed (ignore incomplete, require manifest+checksums). +1.

Allison Grant: LGTM with the note you added re: backup_id in events/logs not as a required metric label.

Connor O'Brien: LGTM. The schema_version / tool_version stuff will save us later.

Diego Santos: Pushed the remaining tweaks:
- Added `wrapped_dek` + wrap provider list
- Added game day evidence note (verify + smoke test output)
If no more blockers, I’ll mark ADR-0137 as Accepted and link it from the Private DR docs.

Marcus Lin: Approved. :white_check_mark:

Hanae Suzuki: :white_check_mark:

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup: :white_check_mark:

Olga Petrov: Approved :white_check_mark:

Allison Grant: :+1:

Connor O'Brien: :shipit:

Diego Santos: Marked Accepted. Thanks all — will reference this in the installer PR(s) and the Confluence runbooks.
